title: Three-step calc chain over a product partition for USA 2020 P3
intent: Reduce the goal ∏A = 2 (the product over a : 1 ≤ a < p with both a and 4−a quadratic non-residues) to a three-step calc chain: rewrite ∏A through the partition C = A ∪ B, erase the element 2, and re-index the erased product onto B, then cancel the common non-zero factor ∏B. Each of the three links and the cancellation hypothesis is a named lemma proved earlier in the same file.

parent.name: usa2020_p3
parent.statement: problem usa2020_p3 (p : ℕ) [hp : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (hp2 : p ≠ 2) : ∏ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun (a : ZMod p) => a ≠ 0 ∧ ¬IsSquare a ∧ ¬IsSquare (4 - a)), a = (solution_val : ZMod p)

children.name: setC_eq_union
children.statement: private lemma setC_eq_union : setC' p = setA' p ∪ setB' p
children.closed_by: ext a; simp [setA', setB', setC', mem_union, mem_filter, mem_univ, true_and]; by_cases on a = 0 and a = 4; rw [isSquare_mul_iff_same p ha (sub_ne_zero_of_ne (Ne.symm ha4))]; tauto

children.name: disjoint_AB
children.statement: private lemma disjoint_AB : Disjoint (setA' p) (setB' p)

children.name: two_mem_setC
children.statement: private lemma two_mem_setC : (2 : ZMod p) ∈ setC' p
children.closed_by: Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, p_two_ne_zero p hp2, p_two_ne_four p hp2, 2, by ring⟩

children.name: prod_C_erase_eq_prod_B
children.statement: private lemma prod_C_erase_eq_prod_B : ∏ n ∈ (setC' p).erase 2, n = ∏ b ∈ setB' p, b
children.closed_by: rw [← Finset.prod_fiberwise_of_maps_to (fun n hn => map_mem_setB p (Finset.mem_of_mem_erase hn) (Finset.ne_of_mem_erase hn)) (fun n => n)]; exact Finset.prod_congr rfl fun _ hb => fiber_prod p hp2 hb

children.name: prod_B_ne_zero
children.statement: private lemma prod_B_ne_zero : ∏ b ∈ setB' p, b ≠ 0

applicability.goal_shape: ∏ a ∈ s, a = c, where s is a Finset filtered by a 'balanced' predicate (here both a and 4 − a are non-squares) so that the complementary set C of the predicate splits as A ∪ B with a fiberwise map n ↦ n · (4 − n) from C \ {2} onto B.
applicability.use_when: the product admits a partition whose parts are related by a re-indexing map, the element to erase and the non-zero factor to cancel are explicit, and each link can be stated as its own lemma with a short proof.
applicability.avoid_when: the re-indexing or the disjointness needs a substantial proof that cannot be stated as a self-contained sibling; the common factor is not provably non-zero; or a link mixes several independent facts so the chain's 'one child per link' shape is forced.

claims.claim: The parent usa2020_p3 closes from the five named lemmas and nothing else project-specific: apply mul_left_cancel₀ (prod_B_ne_zero p) discharges the cancellation, and the three calc links are closed by setC_eq_union together with disjoint_AB (link 1), two_mem_setC (link 2), and prod_C_erase_eq_prod_B (link 3).

claims.claim: The authors state the same three-step plan in a comment above the code: 'C is the disjoint union of A and B. The map n ↦ n * (4 - n) sends C \ {2} to B … Hence ∏ C \ {2} = ∏ B, and cancelling ∏ B ≠ 0 from ∏ A * ∏ B = ∏ C = 2 * ∏ C \ {2} gives ∏ A = 2'.

The file has no sorry, admit, or axiom: all five children and the five supporting lemmas (isSquare_mul_iff_same, p_two_ne_zero, p_two_ne_four, map_mem_setB, fiber_prod) are fully proved, and the file is compiled by lake build in the project's CI on push to main.

consequences: The move creates one rewrite obligation per calc link (three) plus a cancellation obligation, which the glue discharges up front by applying mul_left_cancel₀ (prod_B_ne_zero p) so the rest of the chain is an equality between products. The first link is the only one needing two lemmas at once: setC_eq_union rewrites C as A ∪ B and disjoint_AB is the hypothesis of Finset.prod_union, so forgetting disjointness stalls the one-line rw. The erase step (link 2) depends on two_mem_setC, which in turn needs p_two_ne_zero and p_two_ne_four; the re-indexing step (link 3) hides a depth-3 spine through map_mem_setB and fiber_prod. Failure modes: an unproved non-zero or membership fact collapses a link; the re-indexing is the deep part, so a calc chain that looks flat may still need a non-trivial fiber lemma below the surface.
